assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Cross product
items.clue: Vector operation that sets the direction of dB from a current element.

items.label: Biot–Savart law
items.clue: Gives the small contribution dB from each current element, falling as 1/r².

items.label: Superposition
items.clue: Combining the contributions of separate pieces, with signs from their directions.

items.label: Dipole
items.clue: Kind of source whose B falls as 1/z³, as seen far along the axis of a current ring.

questions.stem: A straight piece of wire 1.0 mm long carries a current of 10 A. Point P is 5.0 cm from the piece of wire, and the line from the wire to P makes an angle of 30° with the direction of the current. Treating the piece of wire as a single current element, what is the magnitude of the magnetic field it produces at P? Use μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A.

Predict first. A student claims that the magnetic field produced by a short straight segment of current-carrying wire has no component parallel to the segment at any point. Which reasoning correctly supports the claim?

options.text: The field points radially away from the segment, and a radial direction is perpendicular to the segment.
The field runs from one side of the segment across to the other, like the field between a magnet's poles.
Each element's field is perpendicular to both the element itself and the line from it to the point.
Parts of the segment ahead of and behind the point produce parallel components that cancel each other.

questions.stem: A straight wire segment 0.30 m long carries a current of 4.0 A. Point P lies on the perpendicular bisector of the segment, 0.20 m from its midpoint. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at P due to the segment? Use μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A.

A closed loop of wire is made of a circular arc of radius 0.10 m that subtends an angle of 240° at its center P, and the straight wire that joins the two ends of the arc. The loop carries a steady current of 5.0 A. Use μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at P?
